blocks.text: Computers work with **values**: numbers (`42`, `3.5`) and text (`"Ali"`). If you give a value a name you can use it again later. That name is called a **variable**.
The `=` sign does not mean "equals", it means **"assign"**: it puts the value on the right into the name on the left. You can calculate with numbers: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`.
A variable's value can be changed later. Above, `apple` was 5 first and then 10.

blocks.prompt: Let `a` be 6 and `b` be 7. Print their product (use `*`).

options: puts the value 5 into the name x
blocks.why: `=` is an assignment: it stores the value under the name.
